QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_20

question.text: 'Chambal Seed Category I AIF' is investing in a pre-revenue deep-tech start-up and chooses to link the valuation to specific technical and commercial targets rather than future forecast. This technique is called:

explanation.text: The Logic: Milestone valuation pegs valuation (and staged funding) to specified technical/commercial milestones in the business plan. Failure to meet a milestone may trigger a downward revision or a 'down round', not automatic withdrawal of funding. The Trap: Weighted average is an anti-dilution method. DCF and book-value are standalone valuation methods but don't 'peg' valuation to milestones. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers milestone valuation. XV (Research Analyst) tests DCF/book-value but not milestone valuation for private markets. Manager's Pro-Tip: Tranche-linked milestones protect the fund from burning too much capital on unproven tech — but frame milestones as OBJECTIVE (e.g., 'ARR of INR 10 crore by Q4 FY26') not SUBJECTIVE ('product-market fit') to avoid interpretive disputes.
